[SP/FA] Octa 1 Monthly Test 2 Review Sheet
Reading · Unit 3 Lesson 1
People use magnets in many ways. What do magnets do?
Magnets pull things with iron in them. They have two poles.
The same poles push each other away.
Different poles pull each other close.

We use magnets every day. Look around you!
They are in lots of things. Compasses have magnets in them.
You can use them to find your way.
Some pencil cases have magnets. So you can close them easily.
Some trains have magnets, too. They can move very fast.
What other things have magnets? Can you find some?
1. What is the best title for the first paragraph?
(A) Two Poles
(B) Pull and Push
(C) Things Without Magnets
(D) How Magnets Work
2. How many poles do magnets have?
(A) one
(B) two
(C) four
(D) six
3. How do the poles in a magnet work?
(A) The same poles make more iron.
(B) The different poles come together.
(C) The same poles pull things.
(D) The poles move very fast.
4. What is true about trains?
(A) Every train has magnets.
(B) Trains with magnets pull other trains.
(C) Trains with magnets push other trains.
(D) Trains with magnets go fast.
5. What does the underlined sentence mean?
(A) You can go a new way.
(B) Compasses tell you the way.
(C) You can use compasses in many ways.
(D) Compasses are on the way.

[SP/FA] Octa 1 Monthly Test 2 Review Sheet
Reading · Unit 3 Lesson 2
In Japan, there is a special train. It is called a maglev train.

A maglev train is very fast. There are magnets in the train and the tracks.
They push each other, so the train lifts above the tracks.
It can move up to 430 kilometers an hour!

Maglev trains are also very quiet and do not make much noise.
So, people can ride comfortably.

Maglev trains help keep the air clean. Magnets make them move.
So, they do not make dangerous gas. They are good for the air.

Maglev trains are great! Do you want to ride one?
1. What is the story mainly about?
(A) how people use trains
(B) how trains make noise
(C) why a maglev train is special
(D) why people make maglev trains
2. What makes maglev trains move fast?
(A) compasses
(B) magnets
(C) gas
(D) air
3. Why can people ride maglev trains comfortably?
(A) They are not dangerous.
(B) They move very fast.
(C) They do not make much noise.
(D) They keep the air clean.
4. What does the underlined sentence mean?
(A) The trains are not dangerous to ride.
(B) Dangerous gas is not good for people.
(C) There is no bad gas from the trains.
(D) The trains do not make much gas.

[SP/FA] Octa 1 Monthly Test 2 Review Sheet
Reading · Unit 4 Lesson 1
Hong Kong is a big city. Houses in Hong Kong are very expensive.
So most people live in small apartments.

Gary Chang is an architect. He makes good use of small spaces.
He uses moving walls. They are on wheels.
He moves the wall in the living room. Then the kitchen appears.

Gary also uses fold-away furniture. At night, he folds away his sofa.
Then his bed appears. It does not take much time.

What a good idea! His apartment does not feel small. Can you believe it?
1. What is the passage mainly about?
(A) how to live in a big city
(B) how to use small spaces well
(C) how to make small furniture
(D) how to move the furniture
2. Why do people live in small apartments?
(A) They like small apartments.
(B) Small apartments are cheap.
(C) Small apartments have a lot of furniture.
(D) They want moving walls.
3. What is Gary's job?
(A) an architect
(B) a waiter
(C) a student
(D) an artist
4. How does Gary make his bed appear?
(A) He folds away his sofa.
(B) He folds away his table.
(C) He pushes the wall in the kitchen.
(D) He pushes the wall in the kitchen.
5. What might we know about fold-away furniture?
(A) It is in big apartments.
(B) It feels very hard.
(C) It can make space.
(D) It is expensive.
